statement: Morteza has 100 sets. Mahdi can choose two and Morteza tells him their intersection and union. Find the minimum number of steps for Mahdi to determine all sets.
For positive integers $a,b$, if $\sigma(a^n)\mid\sigma(b^n)$ for all $n\in\mathbb{N}$, prove every prime factor of $\tau(a)$ divides $\tau(b)$.

In $\triangle ABC$, incircle $\omega$ touches $CB$, $CA$ at $D$, $E$. $X$ is the reflection of $D$ over $B$. $DE$ is tangent to the $A$-excircle at $Z$. The circumcircle of $\triangle XZE$ meets $\omega$ again at $K$. Prove $BK\cap AZ\in\omega$.

Cyclic $ABCD$ with circumcenter $O$, $P=AC\cap BD$. $M$, $N$ midpoints of $AD$, $BC$. $\omega_1,\omega_2,\omega_3$ circumcircles of $\triangle ADP$, $\triangle BCP$, $\triangle OMN$. $E$ is the intersection of $\omega_1,\omega_3$ not on arc $APD$; $F$ for $\omega_2,\omega_3$ not on arc $BPC$. Prove $OE=OF$.
Find all $C\in\mathbb{R}$ such that every integer sequence $\{a_n\}$ bounded below satisfying $0\leq a_{n-1}+Ca_n+a_{n+1}<1$ for all $n\geq 2$ is periodic.

Positive integers $m,n,a_1,\ldots,a_m$. Ali and Mohammad play: Ali picks $b_1,\ldots,b_m\in\mathbb{N}$, then Mohammad picks $s\in\mathbb{N}$ and forms $c_i=a_i+b_{i+s}$. Ali wins if all $c_i$ become divisible by $n$ in finitely many rounds. Find all $m,n$ for which Ali wins regardless of initial values.

Consider a regular $2n$-gon with one longest diagonal parallel to the $x$-axis. Find the smallest $d$ such that a polynomial $P$ of degree $d$ exists whose graph intersects all sides of the polygon at non-vertex points.

In $\triangle ABC$ with $AB<AC$, $I$ is incenter, $E$ is the tangency of the $A$-excircle with $BC$. $F$ on external bisector of $\angle BAC$ with $E,F$ on the same side of $AI$ and $\angle AIF=\angle AEB$. $Q$ on $BC$ with $\angle AIQ=90^\circ$. Circles $\omega_b$, $\omega_c$ tangent to $FQ$ and $AB$, $AC$ at $B$, $C$ respectively, passing through the triangle's interior. If $M$ is the midpoint of arc $BC$ not containing $A$, prove $M$ lies on the radical axis of $\omega_b$ and $\omega_c$.

$n\geq 6$ points in the plane, no three collinear. A road network is a connected graph (edges = segments) with no two edges intersecting except at vertices. Prove there exist three road networks $G_1,G_2,G_3$ with no common edge.
Call $S\subseteq\mathbb{N}$ good if for all distinct $a,b,c\in S$, every positive divisor of $\frac{a^c-b^c}{a-b}$ belongs to $S$. For all $n>1$, prove there exists a good $S$ with $n\notin S$.

An $n\times 2n$ table has some blocked cells. A robot placed on any unblocked cell moves right/left/up/down, changing direction only at blocks or borders. Find the smallest $m$ such that $m$ blocks and a starting cell can be chosen so the robot visits all unblocked cells.

Find all $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathcal{A}$ (closed intervals $[a,b]\subset\mathbb{R}$) satisfying: $x\in f(y)\Leftrightarrow y\in f(x)$; $|x-y|>2\Leftrightarrow f(x)\cap f(y)=\emptyset$; and $f(r)=[r^2-1,r^2+1]$ for $0\leq r\leq 1$.
